reviews.author: MovieGuys
reviews.content:
"Cold Storage" won't be winning any awards, nor is it terribly memorable, but it is fun. 

This is a very downbeat horror action comedy with a fungal zombie vibe that's ridiculous enough to work. It's backed by a cast of down-on-their-luck, likeable characters who very sensibly don't take themselves too seriously. 

The results are quite watchable. I did like the "he's got COVID" moment. It's probably the only point where I would say this film was genuinely funny. That said, there's plenty of action to keep things chugging along. 

In summary, a silly, fun, zombie action flick. Worth a look.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: After a space station’s orbit had disintegrated, one of it’s fuel tanks found it’s way to Western Australia where a deadly fungus was detected by “Quinn” (Liam Neeson) and “Romano” (Lesley Manville). Quickly realising it’s lethal and zombifying toxicity, they ship it back to the States where it is buried deep underground. After many years, this facility is sold off by Uncle Sam and is now one of those storage units for folks with excess junk to keep. It’s here that “Travis” - aka “Teacake” (Joe Keery) does the nightshift with newbie “Naomi” (Georgina Campbell). Having just admitted the elderly “Mrs. Rooney” (Dame Vanessa Redgrave) they settle down to their night’s work. Then he hears a beeping. She hears it too. They investigate. They demolish a wall. Next thing, they are deep in the depths of the former military base where the long forgotten sludge has found itself lots of new friends amongst the bugs and rodents who inhabit the ventilation system. Fleeing for their lives, they call the helpline number on the door and that reactivates the now somewhat older duo who had first discovered it. Armed with seven important items, they must race to the site and save the day before the rain gets to the deadly green stuff and world domination ensues. Though it’s all fairly standard zombie fayre, there are some fun moments as the animal kingdom (especially those of the antlered variety) find themselves infected, and both Neeson and Manville bring an agreeable degree of old-codgerism to their desperate attempts to thwart the bubbling and menacing goo that would have us all combusting. What this might only really be remembered for, though, are the brief appearances from Dame Vanessa. As she approaches her ninetieth year, you have to wonder for how much longer she will be bothered making films at all, let alone daft escapades like this one. If you are just looking for a light-hearted comedy then the affable Keery and Campbell add a little sci-fi; a corrupt boss shifting some dodgy televisions and a jilted lover to these proceedings and you could do a lot worse with films that take themselves more seriously. You will almost certainly never recall it, but it's quite good fun.

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content:
Lots of fun
This is well-acted, superbly casted and has a great mix of cgi and practical effects, prosthetics and makeup to make it look well rounded. It is a fun movie, with good dialogue, characters you get invested in, and a plot that feels urgent. I recommend this a lot, and with Liam delivering his lines perfectly you get the icing on the cake!

reviews.author: JPRetana
reviews.content:
Cold Storage (2026) opens with an intertitle explaining the fate of the Skylab space station. The film informs us that Skylab crashed back to Earth, most of it burning up during reentry. However, one crucial piece survives: an oxygen tank that somehow ends up in a forgotten Australian backwater.

This raises an immediate question. A large piece of a famous space station survives intact, becomes a local tourist attraction, and even attracts media attention (we even see newspaper clippings), yet NASA remains completely unaware of its existence until people begin dying in high numbers and gruesome manners? That seems less like a plot point and more like a failure of basic information gathering.

The authorities eventually (i.e., decades later) respond by dispatching exactly three people to investigate, among them the unfortunately named Dr. Hero Martins. Hero promptly becomes infected by a mind-controlling fungus. At that point it becomes difficult to decide what is most implausible: the fungus’ instantaneous incubation period, its ability to penetrate the thick sole of a boot, or its capacity to communicate with its host in fluent English (ordering her to “spread”).

After this prologue, the film jumps to the present day and introduces its protagonists. The hero, Teacake, is first seen reading The Body Snatchers. The heroine is immediately established as clever enough to recognize that “Teacake” is a literary reference and, more importantly, aware that Teacake is an ex-convict whose employment is a condition of his parole. Counterintuitively, she pressures him into vandalizing the facility they are supposed to be guarding.

The choice to show Teacake reading The Body Snatchers is curious. Were the filmmakers worried audiences might not understand from the opening sequence that they were watching a body-snatcher story? Thanks for the vote of confidence, guys. To be fair, viewers may have forgotten the fungus by this point because it takes remarkably long for anything fungus-related to happen. When it finally does, the results are underwhelming. The fungus either transforms animals into flat, weightless CGI approximations of themselves or causes infected humans to hallucinate things that are obviously digital effects added long after principal photography ended.

Speaking of animals, one of the film’s more intriguing ideas arrives when the protagonists discover a rat king. The heroine explains that the concept dates back to the Middle Ages and is closely associated with plague outbreaks. Assuming that’s factual, it's actually a stronger thematic connection than the Body Snatchers reference. The “Teacake” allusion is even more esoteric, but for those who know, it foreshadows tragic events that run counter to the film’s mostly happy ending.

Anyway, the long mid-stretch is devoted to both leads exhibiting far more resistance to infection than Dr. Hero despite wandering around without hazmat suits (I can only conclude that they buy superior footwear) and to what may be generously termed as character development. Neither protagonist is especially compelling. Near the end, the heroine tells Teacake that he is “more interesting than he looks,” or words to that effect. Simply announcing that a character is interesting does not make him so. Conversely, featuring a Stranger Things actor in yet another Stranger Things knockoff does make him typecast.

At long last, the story arrives at its inevitable climax involving a nuclear device complete with that mainstay of clunky exposition — our old pal the Red Digital Readout, still going strong a quarter into the 21st century. We are assured that the detonation will “irradiate the place” while somehow producing “no atmospheric fallout.” Whether this paradoxical statement has any scientific basis is debatable. In any case, the resulting CGI explosion looks so harmless that it scarcely seems worth worrying about.

The film concludes with a deer vomiting directly toward the camera, a final image intended to tease an inevitable sequel but that only serves as a reminder that the preceding ninety minutes were largely a waste thereof.

Cold Storage wants to be a quirky creature feature, a body-snatcher thriller, and a nostalgic sci-fi horror B comedy that mostly succeeds in being a collection of familiar ideas stitched together with questionable logic, underwhelming visual effects, and characters who never become as interesting as the screenplay insists they are.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: When a dangerous, mutating fungus escapes a subterranean military base, two unlikely facility workers and a veteran bioterror operative must contain the deadly outbreak before it wipes out humanity.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: A top-secret government facility housing a lethal, highly contagious fungal organism suffers a catastrophic containment breach. Trapped inside during an overnight shift, two ordinary employees are forced to team up with a hardened bioterrorism expert to stop the pathogen's rapid spread. Blending dark comedy with sci-fi horror, the trio must overcome absurd obstacles and gruesome threats to prevent a global catastrophe.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Deep beneath the earth, a dormant military facility conceals one of humanity's most dangerous secrets: a rapidly mutating, parasitic fungal strain capable of total ecological destruction. What begins as a routine night shift for two underprepared facility employees turns into a nightmare when an equipment failure breaks containment. As the fungus begins to spread and adapt to its environment, it infects everything in its path, turning the facility into a chaotic hazard zone. Desperate for help, the workers make contact with a grizzled, retired bioterrorism operative who understands the true, terrifying scope of the organism. Arriving at the scene, the operative leads the young staff through dark corridors, grotesque hazards, and spiraling panic. Armed with makeshift weapons and sheer resolve, the improbable team must outsmart the evolving parasite while racing against the clock. Tensions flare as personal drama and dark humor clash with the life-or-death stakes of their mission. Ultimately, they must pull off a dangerous plan to seal the facility and neutralize the threat before the fungus reaches the surface world.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Cold Storage is a genre-bending sci-fi horror comedy that follows two low-level employees working the overnight shift at a decommissioned government facility. Deep in the subterranean vaults lies a highly classified, mutating fungus that has been sealed away for decades. When the temperature controls fail, the parasitic organism awakens and rapidly breaches containment. To stop an impending global extinction event, the two workers must team up with a battle-hardened, cynical bioterrorism expert. Together, this unlikely trio faces a terrifying, hilarious, and desperate night of survival as they attempt to lock down the facility before the deadly outbreak reaches the outside world.

story_structure.climax: The team faces a high-stakes, time-sensitive showdown against the fully unleashed fungal threat to execute a dangerous, last-ditch containment plan.
story_structure.conflict: With the fungus spreading fast and threatening global catastrophe, the duo must team up with a retired bioterrorism operative to contain the organism before it breaches the perimeter.
story_structure.resolution: With the immediate threat neutralized, the survivors deal with the aftermath of their harrowing night shift while humanity narrowly escapes an extinction-level event.
story_structure.introduction: Two low-level employees on an overnight shift at a remote storage facility encounter a deadly, rapidly mutating bio-agent that has escaped containment.
story_structure.risingAction: As the night progresses, the facility plunges into chaos with failing safety protocols, escalating mutations, and perilous environmental hazards forcing the group into increasingly desperate survival situations.

faq.answer: Cold Storage follows two night-shift employees working at a self-storage facility built over an abandoned military site. When a mutating, highly contagious parasitic fungus breaks containment, they team up with a grizzled bioterrorism operative to stop the outbreak and save humanity from extinction.
faq.question: What is the main plot of Cold Storage?

faq.answer: Cold Storage is primarily a sci-fi horror-comedy, blending biological body horror and tense thriller elements with droll action and workplace comedy.
faq.question: What is the dominant genre of Cold Storage?

faq.answer: The film stars Joe Keery and Georgina Campbell as the two night-shift workers, alongside Liam Neeson as the veteran bioterror operative. The supporting cast includes Lesley Manville and Vanessa Redgrave.
faq.question: Who stars in Cold Storage?

faq.answer: Yes, Cold Storage is adapted from the 2019 sci-fi novel of the same name written by veteran screenwriter David Koepp, who also penned the film's screenplay.
faq.question: Is Cold Storage based on a book?

faq.answer: No, Cold Storage is a standalone film and is not connected to any existing movie franchise or shared cinematic universe.
faq.question: Is Cold Storage part of a franchise?

faq.answer: No, Cold Storage is a self-contained story and does not feature any mid-credits or post-credits scenes.
faq.question: Is there a post-credits scene in Cold Storage?

faq.answer: The movie was directed by Jonny Campbell, known for directing television series such as Dracula, Westworld, and Doctor Who.
faq.question: Who directed Cold Storage?

faq.answer: The threat is an explosive, highly contagious space-borne fungal organism stored deep underground decades prior, which reawakens due to temperature changes and infects hosts rapidly.
faq.question: What is the threat facing the characters in Cold Storage?

faq.question: Where does most of the movie take place?
